hypothesis: Along a radius, successive whorl breadths (and hence conch diameters measured at successive half-whorls) of Nautilus, ammonoids and spiral gastropods form a geometric progression: log(diameter) is linear in whorl number, so the whorl expansion rate is constant through ontogeny; for Nautilus the ratio per whole whorl is about 3.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. For every specimen with at least four successive half-whorl conch-diameter measurements (ammonoids: stages with diameter >= 5 mm, excluding the embryonic ammonitella; Nautilus: all measured post-embryonic stages): (1) fit log(dm) against half-whorl index by least squares; the median R^2 across specimens must be >= 0.99, and the exponential (geometric) model must have lower residual sum of squares on the dm scale than a straight-line (arithmetic) model in at least 75% of specimens; (2) strict constancy: the median across specimens of the within-specimen relative range of WER, (max - min)/median over post-embryonic stages, must be <= 0.20, and no systematic ontogenetic drift (median within-specimen Spearman correlation of WER with stage between -0.5 and 0.5); (3) the median Nautilus WER (per-revolution diameter ratio) must lie in [2.6, 3.5]. 'supports' requires (1), (2) and (3).
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. 'refutes' if the geometric model beats the arithmetic model in fewer than 50% of specimens, or the median R^2 < 0.95, or the median Nautilus WER is outside [2.2, 4.0]. 'mixed' if the geometric progression holds approximately ((1) and (3) pass) but the strict constancy test (2) fails, i.e. WER drifts systematically during growth. Gastropods are included only if a public dataset gives successive whorl measurements per specimen; otherwise the gastropod part is reported as data-unavailable and the verdict rests on nautiloids and ammonoids with a caveat.
interpretation: Thompson's 'breadths of successive whorls along a radius in geometric progression' is tested on its equivalent for measured cross-sections: conch diameters at successive half-whorls, whose ratio is constant if and only if the whorl breadths are in geometric progression (both equal e^(pi cot alpha) per half-whorl for a logarithmic spiral). Korn's WER = (dm1/dm2)^2 is that half-whorl ratio squared, i.e. the per-revolution ratio Thompson quotes as 'about three' for Nautilus. The strict reading (a single constant ratio for the whole shell) and the approximate reading (a logarithmic spiral is a very good description) are both pre-registered so that the verdict distinguishes them.
